# Course Overview {.unnumbered}

Lessons are grouped by mathematical object rather than by class day, so some take a single meeting and others span a week.

::: {.timeline-table}
| Weeks | Module | Main topics |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Foundations | Biological sequences as strings; complexity; recurrences; log-odds scoring |
| 2-3 | Pairwise alignment | Global alignment, traceback, correctness, local alignment, affine gaps, seed-and-extend search |
| 4 | Assembly graphs | Reads, k-mers, de Bruijn graphs, Eulerian paths, repeats, sequencing errors |
| 5-7 | Probabilistic sequence models | Sequence likelihoods, Markov chains, CpG islands, HMMs, Viterbi, forward-backward |
| 8-9 | Integration and phylogenetics | Common algorithmic structures, distances, UPGMA, parsimony, Fitch's algorithm |
| 10-11 | Omics matrices and testing | Expression matrices, centering, PCA/SVD, high-throughput testing, FDR |
| 12 | Clustering and single-cell data | Distances, neighborhood graphs, embeddings, single-cell interpretation |
| 13 | Mechanistic models | Gene-regulation ODEs, Hill functions, bistability, toggle switches |
| 14 | Synthesis | Method choice, validation checks, project connections, modern extensions |
:::
